files.README.md:
# Freelancer Get-Paid Kit

Everything you need to send clean invoices, track who owes you what, and chase late payments without awkwardness.

## What's inside

| File | Use it for |
|---|---|
| invoice-tracker.csv | One row per invoice. Open in Excel, Google Sheets or Numbers. |
| invoice-checklist.md | Run through it before every invoice goes out. |
| payment-reminders.md | Four ready-to-send reminder emails, from friendly to final. |
| payment-terms.md | Wording for your proposals and contracts so late payment is less likely. |

## Quick start (15 minutes)

1. Open **invoice-tracker.csv** and delete the three example rows.
2. Add every unpaid invoice you have right now, one per row.
3. Sort by **Due date**. Anything past due gets reminder 1 from **payment-reminders.md** today.
4. Copy the terms you like from **payment-terms.md** into your next proposal.
5. Before each new invoice, run the checklist. It takes two minutes and prevents most payment delays.

## Weekly habit (5 minutes, same day each week)

- Update the **Status** column for anything paid.
- For each overdue invoice, send the next reminder in the sequence and note the date in **Last reminder**.
- Check **Days overdue**. Over 30 days? Move to reminder 3. Over 45? Reminder 4.

## Tracker columns

- **Invoice #**: your own numbering, e.g. 2026-014. Never reuse a number.
- **Client / Project**: who and what.
- **Issued / Due**: dates as YYYY-MM-DD so sorting works everywhere.
- **Amount**: before any tax.
- **Status**: Draft, Sent, Paid, Partial, Overdue, Disputed.
- **Paid on / Paid amount**: fill in when money lands.
- **Days overdue**: in Sheets or Excel, replace the example value with a formula like `=IF(G2="Paid",0,MAX(0,TODAY()-E2))`, adjusting the letters to your columns.
- **Last reminder**: the date and reminder number, e.g. "2026-11-02 (R2)".
- **Notes**: PO numbers, who approves invoices, anything that speeds payment.

files.invoice-checklist.md:
# Invoice checklist

Run this before you hit send. Most late payments come from an invoice that couldn't be processed, not a client who won't pay.

## Who it's going to
- [ ] Sent to the person who actually pays invoices (often accounts or finance), with your contact copied
- [ ] Client's legal business name and address, exactly as they use it
- [ ] Their purchase order (PO) or reference number, if they gave you one

## What's on it
- [ ] A unique invoice number you've never used before
- [ ] Issue date and a clear due date (write the date, not just "Net 30")
- [ ] Each line item matches what you agreed: description, quantity, rate
- [ ] Totals add up, and any tax is shown as its own line
- [ ] Your business name, address and contact email
- [ ] How to pay: bank details or payment link, and who to make it out to
- [ ] Your payment terms, including any late fee you agreed in advance

## Before sending
- [ ] Saved as PDF with a clear filename: `YourName-Invoice-2026-014.pdf`
- [ ] Subject line includes the invoice number and amount
- [ ] Added a row to your tracker with status "Sent"
- [ ] Put the due date in your calendar
files.payment-reminders.md:
# Payment reminder emails

Send them in order. Keep each one short, friendly and specific. Always attach the invoice again: the most common reason for non-payment is that the first email got lost.

Replace everything in [brackets].

---

## Reminder 1: due date passed (send 1-3 days after)

**Subject:** Invoice [#] for [amount] — due [date]

Hi [name],

A quick note that invoice [#] for [amount] was due on [date]. I've attached it again in case the first one went astray.

Could you let me know when I can expect payment, or who I should follow up with?

Thanks,
[your name]

---

## Reminder 2: one week overdue

**Subject:** Following up: invoice [#] ([amount]), now 7 days overdue

Hi [name],

I'm following up on invoice [#] for [amount], which was due on [date]. It's attached again here.

If there's an issue with the invoice, or it needs a PO or approval on your side, just tell me what you need and I'll sort it out today.

Thanks,
[your name]

---

## Reminder 3: 30 days overdue

**Subject:** Invoice [#] is 30 days overdue — please confirm a payment date

Hi [name],

Invoice [#] for [amount] is now 30 days past its due date of [date].

Please reply with a date by which payment will be made. If cash flow is the issue, I'm happy to agree a short payment plan.

Per our agreement, [late fee terms, if any] applies from [date].

Regards,
[your name]

---

## Reminder 4: final notice (45+ days)

**Subject:** Final notice: invoice [#], [amount]

Hi [name],

Despite my earlier emails on [dates], invoice [#] for [amount] remains unpaid, [number] days after it was due.

Please arrange payment by [date, about 7 days out]. If I don't hear from you by then, I'll need to pause any ongoing work and take the next steps to recover the amount owed.

I'd much rather resolve this directly, so please get in touch if there's anything I should know.

Regards,
[your name]

---

## Tips
- Send reminders on Tuesday to Thursday mornings. They get read.
- Call or message after reminder 2 if you have a phone contact. A two-minute call often fixes what four emails can't.
- Stay factual. "It's overdue" works better than "I'm disappointed."
- For anything beyond reminder 4, look up the small-claims or debt-recovery process where you live. Rules differ by country and state.
files.payment-terms.md:
# Payment terms you can copy

Add these to proposals and contracts before work starts. Clients agree to terms more readily up front than after an invoice is late.

## Deposit
> A [30–50]% deposit is due before work begins. The remaining balance is due on delivery.

Good for new clients and one-off projects.

## Due date
> Invoices are due within [14] days of the invoice date.

Shorter terms (7–14 days) get paid faster than "Net 30" for most small clients.

## Late fee
> Invoices unpaid after the due date may incur a late fee of [1.5]% per month on the outstanding balance, where permitted by law.

Check the limits where you and your client are based before using a late fee.

## Work pauses
> If an invoice is more than [14] days overdue, work on the project may pause until the account is brought up to date.

## Milestones (larger projects)
> Payment is made in [3] instalments: [40]% on signing, [30]% at [milestone], and [30]% on final delivery.

## Kill fee
> If the project is cancelled after work has begun, the client will pay for all work completed to date, and no less than [25]% of the total project fee.

## Ownership
> Ownership of final files transfers to the client once payment has been received in full.

This one is powerful and rarely disputed.

---

These are plain-English starting points, not legal advice. For large contracts, have a local professional review your terms.
